title: Customizable Study Space
description: A study space with ambient music, task list, pomodoro timers, and a journal feature to keep track of your study progress!
overlayHTML:
Interactive Essay


May 2025


Note: Best experienced via desktop/laptop!
For my webdev final, I decided to put all I learned into a customizable and interactive study space for students. It has ambient music, an editable task list, and pomodoro timers. Users can change the color scheme of the website however they want, and can log their activity in a journal to keep track of their progress. I really focused on the layout and user experience so it feels cozy and not so daunting because at the time, I was felt very overwhelmed at the prospect of studying. This was a very challenging project and thankfully, our professor allowed us to seek the help of AI. This was one of the first projects where I learned to leverage the debugging and teaching capabilities of AI to help me make my site as polished as possible. I learned about local storage, building timers, and how to target specific elements for a sitewide theme change! There is definitely a lot to be improved but for a 3 week intensive finals sprint I am very happy with how it turned out!

Here is the website!

title: Carnatic Music and Spotify's Algorithm Interactive Essay
description: An interactive essay I made for my Ethics class about Spotify's algorithm and its inaccuracies in analyzing non-western music with an interactive raga visualizer
overlayHTML:
Interactive Essay


Jun 2025


Note: Best experienced via desktop/laptop!
For my Ethics Final, we had a myriad of options, one of which was to develop an essay exploring the implications of an ethical dilemma we discussed in class. I had recently watched a video about Spotify's algorithm and its shortcomings in classifying non-Western music. This reminded me of our discussion of algorithmic bias in the first few weeks of class. However, beyond just writing an essay about it, I wanted to be able to show this bias in play and attempted to use the Spotify Web API to showcase the discrepancies I describe in my essay. Once I wrote the essay, which had various parts beyond just the buttons and HTML content, such as an interactive ragam visulizer to help explain Carnatic Music to non-practitioners and those unfamiliar with it, I realized that the Spotify Web API discontinued the Audio Features aspect of their API. Unfortunately by then I had developed the script for it and decided to turn it in anyways as an essay, but still showcasing my experience with APIs and calling from them.

Here is the website!

title: Audio Visualizer
description: A visualizer for a piece I made for my audio class which had voice, cymbals, and mridangam beats, a prototype for a jathi visualizer I would like to make this into.
overlayHTML:
Audio Visualizer


Apr 2025


Note: Best experienced via desktop/laptop!
In my Audio Foundations class, one of our assignments was to make a song segment that lasted around 30 seconds or so. That project got me thinking about jathis. Jathis are rhythmic patterns that make up the nritta (the abstract movement based aspect) portions of compositions. I wondered if there was a way to visualize the beats because jathis in a performance are performed by the nattuvanar (saying the syllables and hitting the cymbals), the mridangist, and the dancer's footwork. Interestingly enough, even though all follow the same talam cycle (or rhythmic pattern), they fill up the cycle with different beats, using different combinations of beats to reach the same end. What makes this even more interesting is the emphasis on musicality where even though each participant uses different math to fill the talam cycle, they still hold the core of the syllables pronounced. This got me researching into p5.FFT, a very powerful tool that helped me make these distinctions between more bass percussion beats, mid range voice, and high pitched sounds like the cymbals and bells. Once I did this audio project however, I realized that I had something a little more interesting to work with because I could separate my song into different tracks based on instruments and percussion. Using this I began developing a responsive mandala via p5, which I then modified into its own webpage to bring this to life!

title: Character Generator
description: A p5.js sketch of a character generator that allows the user to change or generate outfits of an Indian Princess Doll, a project born out of an analysis of Hayao Miyazaki's work
overlayHTML:
Character Generator



Sept 2024 - November 2024


This project started off as a research project into the creative process of Hayao Miyazaki. The task was to throroughly research the artist's creative process using academic resources and then apply the process into a final product of our choosing. Miyazaki's work was heavily influenced by his childhood, and as I was watching and reading about him and how he generates his ideas, I noticed a very visceral connection to the wonders of childhood. As I ruminated on my childhood, I has a lot of very vivid memories of my younger years in India, my grandfather, and dance. With so much of my childhood being rooted in my heritage, I remembered wearing a lot of ethnic clothing as a child. I also remembered being obsessed with dres up games. Miyazaki tended to start his ideation process by putting pen to paper, and as I did the same, these memories resurfaced. I remember obsessing over Barbie, dressing her up, and suddenly the two clicked. Ethnic clothing and a dress up game. Not to mention, I was also in love with Disney princesses. So I designed a series of tops, bottoms, dupattas and jewelry to formulate this make your own Indian princess dress up game. Originally it was just a series of drawings on Procreate I toggled by layer, but I was encouraged to actually develop it as the final for my creative coding class, where we used p5.js!

HAYAO MIYAZAKI by Srividhya Chandramouleeswaran
